precepts.text: Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel; the same charge, be strong and of good courage.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
David gave Solomon the same charge the Lord gave Joshua: “Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel: be strong, and of good courage; dread not, nor be dismayed.”

Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments; and with it, be strong and of good courage. That is Joshua 1:8: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. The formula for success was handed down from Joshua to the kings of Israel.

precepts.text: David charges the princes of Israel, saying the Lord has given the inhabitants of the land into his hand and the land is subdued before the Lord, which is why Edom had no king of its own in Jehoshaphat's day.
precepts.point: Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
David charged the princes of Israel to help Solomon, saying, “Is not the Lord your God with you? and hath he not given you rest on every side? for he hath given the inhabitants of the land into mine hand; and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people.”

The Most High gave the inhabitants of the land into David’s hand, and the land was subdued. That is why, in Jehoshaphat’s day, “There was then no king in Edom: a deputy was king.” Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted, so it had no king of its own.

precepts.text: Hiram king of Tyre was ever a lover of David, and he sent his servants unto Solomon, helping to supply the timber for the building of the temple.
precepts.point: David prepared iron in abundance for the nails and for the joinings, brass in abundance without weight, and cedar trees in abundance. The Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.” Hiram helped supply the timber for the building of the temple.

That help was already coming in David's day. David gathered the strangers in the land of Israel and set masons to hew stones for the house of God, and prepared iron, brass and “cedar trees in abundance: for the Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.” The strangers were brought in to help build the temple, and Tyre, whose king loved David, kept on helping his son.

precepts.text: The Lord promised David a son, Solomon, who would be a man of rest, having peace and quietness given to Israel in his days.
precepts.point: David had prepared for the house long before, telling Solomon that in his trouble he had laid up a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, brass and iron without weight, timber and stone, and workmen in abundance. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.”

The Lord promised David a son who would be a man of rest, with peace and quietness given to Israel in his days. In that rest Solomon built, setting the strangers in the land to work, “threescore and ten thousand of them to be bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work.”

precepts.text: In his trouble David prepared for the house of the Lord gold, silver, brass, iron, timber, and stone in abundance.
precepts.point: David had prepared for the house long before, telling Solomon that in his trouble he had laid up a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, brass and iron without weight, timber and stone, and workmen in abundance. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Now, behold, in my trouble I have prepared for the house of the Lord an hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver; and of brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance: timber also and stone have I prepared; and thou mayest add thereto.”

David had prepared for the house long before. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials. Even the numbering of the strangers was “after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them.”

points: David said, This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar of the burnt offering for Israel. He commanded to gather together the strangers that were in the land of Israel and set masons to hew wrought stones to build the house of God. These strangers were brought in to help with the building of the temple.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: David prepared iron in abundance for the nails and for the joinings, brass in abundance without weight, and cedar trees in abundance. The Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: David said that Solomon his son was young and tender, and the house to be built for the Lord must be exceeding magnifical, of fame and glory throughout all countries, so he prepared abundantly before his death.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: He called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: David told Solomon that it was in his mind to build a house unto the name of the Lord, but the word of the Lord came to him saying he should not build it because he had shed blood abundantly and made great wars. Because of all the wars and fighting David had done, the Most High did not allow him to build the temple.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: The Lord promised David a son who would be a man of rest, to whom he would give rest from all his enemies round about, whose name would be Solomon, and in whose days he would give peace and quietness unto Israel. This son would build the house for the Most High's name, and the Most High would establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: David charged Solomon that the Lord be with him and prosper him to build the house of the Lord his God, and asked that the Lord give him wisdom and understanding and charge concerning Israel that he might keep the law of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: He said Solomon would prosper if he took heed to fulfill the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel. This is the same message the Most High gives us today: we will prosper as long as we obey the commandments. Be strong and of good courage; dread not, nor be dismayed.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: In his trouble David prepared for the house of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold and a thousand thousand talents of silver, and brass and iron without weight, and timber and stone in abundance, telling Solomon he might add thereto. Without weight means they gave in such abundance they were not counting it.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: There were workmen with him in abundance, hewers and workers of stone and timber and all manner of cunning men for every kind of work. David told Solomon to arise and be doing, and the Lord be with him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: David commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, asking whether the Lord their God was not with them and had not given them rest on every side, for he had given the inhabitants of the land into David's hand and the land was subdued before the Lord. This is what David was there to do: he subdued all the nations by the power of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

points: He charged them to set their heart and soul to seek the Lord their God, to arise and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, and to bring the ark of the covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that was to be built. Earlier David had moved the ark from place to place, and that is when he desired to build a house for it before the Lord.
